channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Iran preparing response to US, says Washington must 'honor commitments'
item.description: Iran says it is finalizing its response to the US through mediators, accusing Washington of failing to honor commitments as talks over the Strait of Hormuz stall.

item.title: UK announces public inquiry into Yom Kippur synagogue attack
item.description: Britain launches a public inquiry into the 2025 Manchester synagogue terror attack in which two Jewish worshippers were murdered.

item.title: One dead in roller coaster incident at Six Flags in Georgia
item.description: One person is dead and several others injured following a roller coaster incident at Six Flags Over Georgia. Police investigating.

item.title: Trump confirms: Administration considering removing US Ambassador to Greece
item.description:
US President Donald Trump confirmed that his administration is considering removing US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle following reports concerning her conduct.
"We're looking into it. Yes, we're not happy," Trump told reporters. Earlier, The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were considering dismissing Guilfoyle, after Greek and American businesspeople allegedly financed luxury trips for Guilfoyle in exchange for her assistance in advancing their interests.

item.title: Federal agents raid Ilhan Omar's home amid immigration fraud investigation
item.description: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home amid an immigration fraud investigation. Omar accuses Trump of intimidation; he denies involvement.

item.title: Trump: Midterm elections won't affect Iran policy, war will end soon
item.description: President Trump says the midterm elections will not change his Iran policy, predicts the war will end soon, and criticizes Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Hungarian University honors Gaza terrorist, then removes tribute
item.description: Gaza terrorist honored by a Hungarian university as an outstanding student killed in the war. An Israeli exposes his terrorist activities, prompting the removal of the tribute.

item.title: Prof. Anne Bayefsky: 'Navi Pillay turned Jew-hate into golden ticket'
item.description: In a statement to Arutz Sheva, Professor Anne Bayefsky accuses the Nobel Committee of rewarding anti-Israel hostility and warns that the decision sends a dangerous message to international lawyers.

item.title: Israel showcases combat-proven defense technology at major US exhibition
item.description: Amid record defense exports exceeding $19.2 billion, Israel's Defense Ministry brings 19 companies to AUSA 2026 in Washington, showcasing advanced drone interception, electronic warfare, and AI-powered surveillance technologies.

item.title: Indonesian pilot identified en route to Israel: Cargo plane forced to return to Ethiopia
item.description: An Ethiopian Airlines cargo flight to Tel Aviv returned to Ethiopia after one of its pilots was identified as an Indonesian citizen. The pilot was replaced, and the flight resumed.

item.title: Elegy and anthem for a Hilltop they can’t keep down
item.description: Requiem for our national sanity. Every outpost we demolish is a gift to the people who dream of looking down on the coastal plain from these ridges. We are giving aid and comfort to the enemy, and we are doing it at our own mortal expense. Opinion.

item.title: President Herzog awards Presidential Medal of Honor to Israel Bonds
item.description: President Isaac Herzog honors Israel Bonds for raising more than $58 billion over 75 years, including $8.5 billion since October 7.

item.title: Two polls: Hendel and Zelekha cross electoral threshold; Ofer Winter is out
item.description: The Reservists-Economic Party, led by Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha, wins four seats in two polls published this evening, while Amcha Yisrael Party, led by Ofer Winter, remains below the electoral threshold.

item.title: Report: Explosions heard in Saudi capital Riyadh
item.description: According to initial reports, explosions were heard in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Injured student recounts: 'He unscrewed it - and then it exploded'
item.description: Eitan Masaori, a student injured by shrapnel in his neck, told the PM that another student had been playing with the munition before the explosion.

item.title: Cyber ​​attack in France: Hackers raised temperatures in refrigerators, causing fires
item.description:
A large-scale cyberattack hit hundreds of supermarkets across France overnight, after hackers caused the temperature in networked refrigerators to rise to 50 degrees Celsius.
As a result, fires broke out and food products were damaged in many stores.

item.title: Three foreign activists to be deported after filming IDF soldiers in Hevron
item.description: Three foreign activists, including the president of an anti-Israel organization that promotes BDS, who filmed IDF soldiers in Hebron will be deported from Israel after photos of soldiers from previous shifts were found.

item.title: Herzog slams deicison to award Navi Pillay the Nobel Peace Prize
item.description:
President Isaac Herzog sharply criticized the decision to award the Nobel Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, which he said is "one of the most prominent proponents of the lie about genocide."
Herzog called the decision "cynical" and claimed that it expressed "moral erosion" and constituted "an insult to every person who sanctifies life and seeks peace, and in particular to the victims and survivors of the October 7 murders."

item.title: Disturbing footage: Cyclist thrown onto road in collision
item.description: Security camera footage captured the moment an electric bicycle rider collided with a car in Bnei Brak.

item.title: Three years of lies and slander
item.description: While Evyatar David was being tortured, starved, and forced to dig his own grave, someone slandering his rescuers as "genocidal" is a barbarian. And if a months-old baby is murdered with bare hands by his captors, as Kfir Bibas was, someone slandering his rescuers is simply a monster. Opinion.

item.title: UK imposes sanctions on two Iranian officials for espionage
item.description:
Britain announced the imposition of sanctions against two elements of the Iranian regime for their involvement in espionage activities for Iran.
One of them is a senior member of the Revolutionary Guards, and the other is linked to a network that works to harm opponents of the Iranian regime.

item.title: 'I will not give in': Katz draws a red line for the High Court over Judea and Samaria
item.description: Katz warns the High Court against intervening in IDF’s activities in northern Samaria refugee camps, vows to maintain IDF presence, even if special legislation is needed.

item.title: US, Australia, Canada and other countries issue joint statement against Iran
item.description:
The United States, Australia, Canada and other countries issued a joint statement against Iranian activity on their territory.
The statement said that "any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass or harm people on our territory, through proxies or by any other means, is unacceptable."

item.title: Bezalel Smotrich: 'I pray that God leads him to repent as well'
item.description: Smotrich says failed draft law would have brought thousands of haredim into the IDF, adding that he prays Rabbi Dov Lando will repent.

item.title: Israel’s enemies never let up or fail to shock
item.description: Ahead of the Oct 7 anniversary, Britain’s Green party shockers hitched their wagon to The Holocaust creed: Jews have forfeited the right to exist. Modern antisemitic movements have mastered the playbook (for manipulating human nature. Opinion.
